draft.shortGloss: to get angry; to be upset
draft.emotion: frustrated and upset, bubbling over with sudden irritation
notes: Formed from 화 (anger) + 나다 (to come out), and often used as two words with a subject particle: 화가 나다. In the present tense to mean 'I am angry right now', Korean commonly uses the past form 화났어요 ('I have gotten angry').
Do not confuse with 화내다 (화를 내다), which means to actively show or express anger toward someone.

senses.definition: To come to feel strong displeasure or anger.

examples.translation: I got really angry because he lied.
